newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIA LAUNCHES NEW BUSINESS GROUP.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIA LAUNCHES NEW BUSINESS GROUP.

text.p: A new consortium called Europe has sprung from Bulgaria's most powerful conglomerate Multigroup with businesses focusing on food production, medical supplies, art, printing and security, officials said on Wednesday.

"Access to the consortium is open for everyone who shares our business philosophy: to work, profit and invest in Bulgaria," Dimitar Ivanov, board chairman of Consortium Europe told a news conference, also attended by businessmen and intellectuals.
"I have borrowed many of the financial management and accounting techniques from Multigroup, where I previously worked," said Ivanov, who until mid-1996 was vice-president of Multigroup.

One of a small handful of powerful firms to have sprung up in Bulgaria amid the legal and administrative chaos that followed the collapse of communism, Multigroup has sometimes attracted negative publicity.

The interests of Multigroup, the Bulgarian branch of Liechtenstein-registered Multiinternational Holding Ltd, range from oil and gas distribution in the Balkans to trading raw materials such as metals and sugar.

"We are not interested in oil trade, communication or satellite technology. We are interested in art, printing and catering to social needs such as food production and medical treatment," said Ivanov, who is also the founder of a local oil trading company Ares.
A branch of Ares, now part of the Europe Consortium, is involved in collection and restoration of antiques and archeological research.
One of the biggest companies in the group, Step, has a monthly turnover of 200,000 from stockbreeding, wheat and meat production, said Ivanov.
"We have set the Consortium to join efforts and overcome the current crisis" said Ivanov, who under Bulgaria's pre-1989 communist regime headed the surveillance department of the secret police.

Analysts frequently attribute Bulgaria's current unprecedented economic crisis to asset stripping of profitable state companies and syphoning of funds abroad by businesmen from the former Communist Party in the past six years.

Consortium Europe has offices in Austria, Greece, USA, Russia and Cyprus. It comprises 16 companies whose activity ranges from company security and import of medical equipment to food production. -- Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-84561
